newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl welcomes Yeltsin at start of German visit.
newsitem.headline: Kohl welcomes Yeltsin at start of German visit.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl welcomed Russian President Boris Yeltsin to Germany on Thursday at the start of a day of talks in the historic spa town of Baden-Baden.
Kohl went to Yeltsin's hotel to greet the president and his wife before receiving him formally with full military honours in an elegant park bright with spring sunshine.

Yeltsin looked pale and somewhat tired as the two men shook hands. They drove from the hotel to the park in a motorcade, although their programme had said they would walk if the weather was fine. Neither man made any comments.

The two men's discussions, taking place over a lengthy working lunch at a nearby country restaurant, were likely to focus on attempts to secure an agreement between NATO and Russia which gives Moscow influence on the alliance as it expands eastwards.

Also on the agenda was the vexed question of the art works seized by the Soviet army from vanquished Germany at the end of World War Two. Bonn wants the treasures back while the communist-dominated Russian parliament sees them as legitimate compensation for the damage the Nazis inflicted.
Yeltsin's entourage included his wife Naina, his younger daughter Tatyana Dyachenko, appearing for the first time in such a public role abroad, and chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov.
The talks were due to begin at 1020 GMT, and to be followed by a news conference at 1415 GMT.
